name: threeseven
title: Daytona: Three Seven Speedway
note: Daytona USA (1994, Model 2), Beginner course, imported as is: the original polygons and tiles (export of tools/import/daytona/tracks/rom/daytona_export.py), nothing added or rounded. Build: python import_classic.py daytona 1 classic --norender --name step99_daytona_threeseven_desert4 (export_adapter.py turns the export into the importer's input files).
centreline_note: the export's centre line = the mean of the eight driving lines, in game axes (the SRC files are in the OBJ's axes, Z negated)
start_note: at = the middle of the yellow start / finish line under the start gantry (tile tex_s1_x0768_y0032_256x32_c250_p0_t, game x / z); Daytona's own grid was not found in the ROM: SR3's two-column grid (Lakeside's distances, 3 m either side of the centre line)
ai_lines_note: the eight driving lines of the course directory (daytona_usa_rom_data.md section 7) as the eight lanes of the AI map
boundary_note: Follow every physical road slice without an inset, using the exposed footprint boundary. The former four-slice chords and 0.5 m inset obstructed the banking. The separate outer-side edge_visual_right correction restores support under existing asphalt where the former 30 cm comparison falsely pinched the road; scenery, inner curb and AI route are unchanged.
max_left_note: the inner edge held at 25 m: at most 38 quads across, as SEGA's widest. Rally.exe takes at most A + 1 + B = 132 vertex records per road slice (0x4ECE60, build_testtrack.road_width_check: about 64 quads across); the full width (83) wrote past that buffer and crashed while loading. This narrow form loads and races (in game, 2026-10-14)
edge_visual_note: 40 cm on the outer (positive-column) asphalt side matches the actual discrepancy between the original banked asphalt and coprocessor collision triangulations. At 30 cm a few twisted asphalt faces falsely stop the width walk, producing 3.5 m half-width pinches spread by the edge-rate limiter. Upright wall/kerb blocking remains enabled; 40 and 50 cm produce identical widths. The inner curb keeps its original 30 cm rule and 25 m cap; no inner support changes.
road_width_note: the drivable road = Daytona's collision quads (coprocessor ROM) where the visible ground lies on them and nothing stands across them: the collision runs on under the outer walls and under the 1 m kerb of the inner grass, so the road ends at their foot (edge_visual). The heights are then those of the drawn scenery where it lies within 35 cm of the collision (road_height_visible: Daytona's road polygons and collision quads differ by up to 0.3 m on the banking, 99 % within 10 cm), so the wheels sit on what is seen. The banking rises 0.6 m a metre (road_height_slope). Inside the bottom bend the infield grass is drivable up to 70 m from the centre line (max_half_width)
surface_note: Daytona's collision has no surface field: the road columns whose visible ground is the infield grass tile take code 200 = the second layer pair (Lakeside4's grass), everything else is tarmac
road_layers_note: Alpine4's Terrain_Tarmac pair (clean tarmac, as Mountain); Lakeside4's WetMud_Base + Lakeside_Grass_Top for the grass
pace_notes_note: no co-driver calls: the original has none (the geometry alone gave one HAIRPINLEFT a lap)
splits_note: Daytona's Beginner course has no checkpoints (only the line): SR3's two markers a lap, as the slot's own records have them (the gate just after the line, and half a lap)
arcade_times_note: seconds at marker 1 / 2 (easy, normal, hard); lap 1's first value is the time at the start. A guess for a 1.55 km lap of about 30 s: Daytona's own time table was not decoded
props_note: the slot's animals, props and breakables go (authored empty object list) and so does their model file (gameobj_gfx_dis_data: the loader skips it when missing, as in the 'minimal' form that loaded in game); the pobj files, the grass cache and the cameras stay (the game needs them, 21_track_install_and_switching.md section 6)
gates_note: Daytona's own start gantry is part of the course model; no SR3 or 1995 gate is added
sky_note: Daytona's sky is a 2D scroll layer that was not extracted: the slot's own sky dome stays (its far horizon card is removed)
lighting_note: Mountain's RAW light: flat-lit tiles (Daytona's are baked flat at 0.7 diffuse by the exporter), Tropical4's lighting sets for the cars
resolve_on_surface_note: the resolver's pieces of a twisted polygon (the banking's quads) stay on its drawn surface instead of its best plane, where they left cracks of a few cm along the neighbours' edges
coplanar_note: the 425 tyre-mark polygons (tex_s1_x0768_y0256_128x32_c23D_p0_t) lie 4.4 .. 5.0 cm over the asphalt (Model 2 draws them by priority); a long one on the curved banking up to some 30 cm off the planes of the road faces under it: resolved in the road's plane (composed into its tiles) instead of being lifted further off it
stitch_note: seal1995.py (the hairline / T-joint seal of Mountain's RT builds) does not settle on this course: 17 000, then 18 000, then 134 000 corners on edges in its three passes, 750 000 triangles added (long road strips cut by uv_split and the resolver into thin pieces, whose fans make new joints). Left off, as in Mountain's RAW: some 17 000 corners lie on a neighbour's edge (Mountain RAW: 8 000); the cracks of a few cm that were seen came from twisted faces cut in their best plane and are cured by resolve_on_surface
atlas_note: the game holds 1024 distinct textures in all (track, cars, HUD, sky: 0x585D10, int3 at 0x585D5C when full); the first build had 797 for the track alone and stopped while loading. Pictures that never repeat across a polygon (the resolver's composed region pictures, cut-outs within one repeat, one-colour pictures) go onto shared 1024 x 1024 pages, texel for texel, with a 16-texel border (atlas1995.py)
checker_note: the 277 polygons of colour col_c26E_p3_ck are drawn by the Model 2 every other pixel (the wire fences on the outer walls): alpha-blended at 50 %
